chapter: Moving, Columbia Missouri and leaving home
title: Why the blues cannot be explained or imitated; music of 1975
summary: He says original jazz came from hard lives, today's music reflects confusion, and that bitterness requires dissonance and distortion.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Well, that's a very interesting comment, and wouldn't you like to talk a little more about that, since your music is an expression of what is inside you and what's inside you is an expression of what you encounter in life?

Yes, of course. As I was saying about description of this blues, I think that it's very difficult to categorize music, it's very difficult to explain music, particularly to someone who doesn't know anything about

music. And I think even a discussion of notes, sharps, and flats have very little to do with music except that it's the way to play a note. You know, it's like a carpenter who learns how to drive a nail, but it doesn't necessarily tell him to where to put the nail, see.
Right.

And I'm sure that the original jazz and blues that was created by the great players of jazz music came about by the lives they had to live, which was similar to the situation I'm telling you about now that made me leave home. And by this same token, is the reason why someone who has not lived that particular life could never possibly give the expression of this type of music as someone who lived it. You see?
Yes.

So consequently there has been a change in the music you might say according to the change of times. And I think as the times have become confusing, in 1975, by virtue of all of the strife and struggles of that period, the music is in the same particular vein.
It reflects it.

It reflects the same thing, because there seems to be a constant struggle of people to find maybe their identity or to find peace of mind and in other words life goes on no matter what era. People have the blues and

people are unhappy and they are dissatisfied, and they haven't found any new way, I don't think, of really expressing these things. But in trying to express it in a new way, they have sort of distorted the true meaning in music.
Because actually there is a certain beauty in expression of the blues which has some sadness to it. But there I don't think is any way to express violence or bitterness unless you play bitter.
Yes.
Bitter sounds.
Yes.
You know?
Right.
Dissonant sounds.
Yes. Right.
Distortions.
Disturbed.
Loud. No shading of color. You know?
Yes, right.
Perhaps that might explain why there's so much difficulty in the younger musicians, or the musicians of this present era to express music with beauty as well as sadness.
Yes,yes, I think that's very true.
But without getting hooked up too far
into that I just thought I would mention that part because I think it's informative and interesting.
It is.
As I say about many things that I do say, --
